A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same reweighted diffusion-sampling work, despite substantial revision and renaming. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. V1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–C were included.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original synthetic-distribution experiments, CSI compression analysis, CelebA class reweighting and StableCascade image-generation results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original synthetic sampling, SD/SDXL preference alignment, ablations, MNIST class reweighting and image-control results.

M1.justification: The finite-difference guidance approximation is retained, but v2 adds time-dependent guidance scaling through the LAGS scheduler in Section 3.3 and a hard-gating alternative in Appendix B.2. Appendix C.2.2 also implements an optional projection of guidance perpendicular to the DDIM drift. These additions change the sampling procedure beyond the ISSGM-to-LAGS renaming.

E1.justification: V2 replaces the Circles, Spiral, Pinwheel and 8-Gaussians benchmarks with a 25-Gaussian base distribution and shaped target distributions, and removes the CSI compression task. It adds SD/SDXL human-preference alignment and MNIST class suppression/balancing. CelebA and StableCascade frequency control remain, with additional RGB-bias and low-frequency-control scenarios.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates MADE-MAA, NIS, NSF, CSF and TNA in Table 1; these comparisons disappear. V2 evaluates DPS, FreeDoM and DAS in the synthetic comparisons, and additionally DAS-1p in image alignment. DPS was previously cited but not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: V1's synthetic evaluation uses Jensen–Shannon divergence and DDPM-based SDE sampling. V2 introduces DDIM evaluation using Wasserstein distance and runtime for 10,000 generated samples. The new image-alignment protocol specifies 100 diffusion steps, shared 8×PickScore weighting, and multiple alignment, perceptual-quality and diversity metrics. These are new evaluation designs, not evidence of same-setting reruns.

E4.justification: V2 adds scheduler-coefficient sensitivity studies, projected versus standard guidance comparisons, reward–diversity analysis and qualitative investigations of alignment versus realism in Appendix C.2. These substantially extend the analysis beyond v1's demonstrations. Conversely, v1's CSI high-distortion failure analysis is removed.

E5.justification: V1 reports unexplained ± quantities in its synthetic-results table. V2 explicitly identifies mean ± standard deviation in Tables 1 and 4 and newly documents matched seeds or noise for paired visual comparisons. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or significance testing; the additional reporting does not establish that more runs were performed.

E6.justification: V1's synthetic divergence results and Spiral/CSI/StableCascade mean-weight entries disappear. V2 adds WD/runtime, preference, quality, diversity and MNIST results: Figure 1 reports LAGS WD 0.33, and Table 1 reports 85 seconds per SDXL image versus 4.722 times that runtime for DAS. These are new-setting results. CelebA's 35.1% to 51.2% result and the original StableCascade frequency examples are retained.

T1.justification: V1 states Theorem 1 without a proof and assumes an approximate second-order expansion. V2 revises the assumptions, including bounded support and a bounded Hessian of the weight itself, changes the error bound and supplies a proof in Appendix B.1. It adds Proposition 1 under an error-orthogonality assumption, plus a hard-gating derivation without that assumption.

C1.justification: V1 claims the first training-free score-based importance-sampling framework and emphasizes industrial and natural-image applications. V2 drops that priority claim and centers its contributions on lightweight guidance plus uncertainty-adaptive scheduling. Its abstract and introduction now claim matching or superior task performance with approximately 1.2–4.7× speedups over competing guidance methods.

C2.justification: V2 extends the approximation-error discussion into an explanation of early-step instability and guidance scheduling. Appendix C.2 introduces substantive interpretations of reward–diversity and reward–realism tradeoffs, metric disagreement and projection effects. Comparisons are explicitly restricted to training-free guidance, while v1's CSI failure-mechanism interpretation is removed.

D1.justification: Appendices B.3 and C add discrete sampling updates, noise schedules, architecture specifications, optimizer settings, training budgets, weight formulas and baseline configurations. Retained CelebA and StableCascade experiments receive checkpoint, classifier-training and Fourier-mask details absent from v1. The listed source-code repository address also changes; its availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V1 stresses separation from conditional sampling and says no prior baselines exist for its setup. V2 instead explains connections and adaptations to posterior guidance, positioning the contribution around inference efficiency. Appendix A substantially expands related work, including FreeDoM, DAS, particle sampling and fairness; Appendix C also introduces Adaptive Projected Guidance.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and conclusion around guidance efficiency, reorganizes the method and experimental narrative, and changes terminology from importance sampling/ISSGM to weighted sampling/LAGS. Retained applications move into structured appendices, accompanied by expanded explanations and a contents page.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with new density/runtime panels, alignment plots, sensitivity curves, quality/diversity tables and image grids. V1 Figures 4 and 5 reappear as v2 Figures 13 and 21 with presentation changes. The conceptual, Spiral and CSI figures and original table structures are removed.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses a central weakness of v1 by comparing against competing training-free guidance methods, with explicit runtime and quality evidence, rather than relying on separately trained density models. Added proofs, sensitivity/tradeoff analyses and implementation details substantially strengthen the paper's support and reproducibility. Removing CSI narrows application evidence, and some superiority claims remain overstated: Figure 6's rings example favors FreeDoM at WD 0.37 over LAGS at 0.48 despite its caption. These shortcomings temper but do not outweigh the substantial gains.
